thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: High error rate on serving-runtime — repeated 'CUDA illegal memory access' crashes on node serving-node-23. Spike started ~4999997700. Auto-evac attempted.

sam (ops-oncall): seeing the same. Metrics: 5xx up to 12% for model /gpt-embed-prod, node shows repeated container restarts.

jordan (sre): copying recent `dmesg` from node: ```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=4132 illegal device address 0x7f8a...
kern: device 65:00 illegal memory access at 0x7f8a12ac (pc 0x7f8a34ff)
```

maria (eng-runtime): stack trace in container logs points to our attention kernels during KV cache restore path. Also seeing `cudaMemcpy` failure followed by SIGSEGV in the runtime.

kevin (runtime): this smells like the pointer-offset race we've seen in the testbench where pagewalks and SMMU translations occasionally return misaligned device addresses. Not identical but similar symptoms. Can we repro with the same workload?

sam (ops-oncall): immediate mitigation steps: cordon + drain serving-node-23, scale up fallback pool (cpu-fallback nodes) and route canary traffic there. `kubectl cordon serving-node-23 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data serving-node-23`

liz (support): CS asked for customer impact note — a handful of customers (3) on this shard saw transient 5xx between 12:17-12:22 UTC, most requests retried and succeeded. I'll draft a short blurb.

jordan (sre): draining now. also enabling node-level nvidia-driver telemetry to capture `addr` values. Keep node out of autoscaler so it doesn't rejoin.

maria (eng-runtime): quick hot mitigation we can try: disable prefix KV restore on startup for that node pool (forces cold warmup but avoids corrupt offset reads). Pushing config flag now to `dedicated-pool-v2`

kevin (runtime): if it's a kernel/VMM translation bug we should also try running the same model on a different device type (different GPU series) to see if it's hardware/driver specific. Spinning up two pods on ggpu-b/ggpu-c now.

qa-bot: automated smoke tests triggered against ggpu-b cluster — 30 minute run. Will report failures to this thread.

jordan (sre): got a partial repro locally under stress: after ~2k concurrent sessions a single process produced `illegal device address` and then container OOMed. Stack shows: ```#0 0x7f8a34ff in nv_kernel_compute+0x...
#1 0x7f8a12ac in cuda_kv_restore+0x...
```

sam (ops-oncall): rolling a node-level kernel-driver restart isn't acceptable for customer impact right now. Prioritize draining + fallback.

maria (eng-runtime): started a canary where we force `--quantize-mode=fp16` instead of int8 for that pool (different memory paths). Early telemetry: no crashes so far across ~400 requests.

kevin (runtime): interesting — suggests a quantization IPC path triggers different kernel paths. Need full logs and device addresses when it happens. Jordan, can you enable core dumps and upload to artifact store?

jordan (sre): yes. `echo /tmp/cores/core.%e.%p.%t > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` and increased `ulimit -c unlimited` on the test node. Upload in 30m if repro.

liz (support): drafted customer message: "We observed transient errors affecting a small set of requests between 12:17-12:30 UTC due to a GPU driver/kernel issue. Traffic was automatically routed to fallback capacity and most requests retried successfully. Engineering is investigating root cause. We'll update shortly." Any objections? :thinking:

cs-lead: fine to send. Add an ETA for next update in 60 minutes.

qa-bot: smoke tests on ggpu-b started failing at test 14 with `CUDA illegal memory access` — recording test vector and payload.

maria (eng-runtime): pulling the failing test vector. Looks like a long prefix with repeated attention windows ~3k tokens triggers the repro. That matches the KV cache boundary suspicion.

kevin (runtime): plan: 1) keep node cordoned/drained, 2) route critical traffic to dedicated fallback pool, 3) disable KV-prefetch/restore on affected pool, 4) run repro harness against ggpu-b and capture coredump + nvstack, 5) if repro is deterministic, prepare a hotfix in runtime to add sanitizer around pointer arithmetic and guard misaligned addresses.

sam (ops-oncall): executing plan steps 1-3 now. Scaling fallback pool x1.5.

jordan (sre): uploaded a core dump and attached nvprof + `nvidia-smi` status. Artifact: s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/4999997777/core-serving-node-23.tgz

maria (eng-runtime): download started. Initial analysis: pointer that becomes misaligned is coming from a host-to-device translation in the SMMU layer. Could be driver or VMM. We're opening MR for added bounds checks in runtime to avoid immediate crash; we'll stage to canary.

kevin (runtime): timeline: if hotfix passes canary in 2-3 hours we can roll to affected pool. If not, longer mitigation is to keep KV-restore disabled for one week while we do deeper driver tests with GPU vendor.

liz (support): customer update sent with ETA. Monitoring ticket ids: #INC-4999997, #CS-8821

cs-lead: good. Keep customer comms at least hourly until resolved.

jordan (sre): note — we saw one node rejoin silently because autoscaler rebalanced. I've put a temporary cluster policy to prevent rejoin until we mark the node safe.

maria (eng-runtime): hotfix MR created: `runtime: guard kv-restore pointer offsets (panic -> safe-fallback)` — PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281. Requesting expedited review.

kevin (runtime): i'll review asap. Add unit tests around misaligned offsets.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: traffic routing changed -> 100% of affected shard moved to fallback pool at 4999997815, error rate dropped to ~0.3%.

sam (ops-oncall): continuing to monitor. If we see any crash in fallback pool, escalate to emergency.

maria (eng-runtime): canary push of MR to `dedicated-pool-v2` started at 4999997840. No crashes in first 2000 requests.

qa-bot: smoke run finished on ggpu-b — 2 failures out of 5400 requests, logs attached to artifact store.

kevin (runtime): next steps for root cause: vendor debug session with GPU driver team + kernel SMMU logs, reproduce against different driver versions, and a runtime-level sanitizer to catch illegal device addresses early.

cs-lead: capture postmortem scope: timeline, customer impact, mitigation, root cause hypothesis (SMMU/driver pointer translation race), and follow-ups (hotfix roll, vendor escalation, test coverage). Assign owners and ETA for postmortem draft in 48h.

sam (ops-oncall): leaving a note for oncall handoff: next oncall is jordan at 5000001400. Please monitor alerts and customer tickets.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. will update this thread with hotfix rollout results.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> reduced customer impact. Incident remains open for root cause analysis.
